title: Critique: Newman’s problem, a purely formal description is near vacuous

statements.text: Max Newman, replying to Russell’s Analysis of Matter, showed that any purely formal description of the physical world is near vacuous: given enough objects, set theory supplies relations of any structure, so the description says little more than how many objects there are. A theory avoids this only with at least one non-formal notion, such as a causal or nomic one.

sources.quote: The essence of the problem is that any purely formal description of the physical world is near vacuous.
We can avoid Newman’s problem only if our theory of the world contains at least one non-formal (i.e. non-logico-mathematical) notion.
